I actually used to work at Lexmark as a software developer back in the late 90s, and even back then, I found the whole concept of the inkjet model -- basically selling the printer at cost and making money on ink cartridges that are designed to fail early and often -- disgusting. What killed it for me was that I worked on laser printers, which were so much inherently better, but they were never going to try and make a really affordable consumer / desktop laser because inkjets could be so much more profitable.

I quit working in the printer business in 2000 because, frankly, it was boring. Even back then, most of the "new technology" going into printers was just buzzword salad -- look, a laser printer that runs Linux as its embedded OS. Who cares what it runs, it just needs to print. All the interesting problems in that industry were solved long ago, and since the turn of the century the only real innovation is how to slap DRM onto consumables. It's frankly grotesque.
